notes: Baga, its highly acidic and tannic grape, is used for both red and sparkling wine.
Port is usually a sweet red, fortified with grape spirit that stops fermentation, giving 19 to 22% alcohol.
It has intense aroma, rich fruit and high sweetness, from small, dense grapes with concentrated flavor.
Ruby ports are aged briefly in large vessels to keep their bright red color and full fruit.
Tawny ports age in wooden barrels, slowly oxidizing to a golden-brown color with nutty flavors.
White port is made from white grapes in dry to very sweet styles.
White Vinho Verde is very fresh from natural acidity, with fruity and floral aromas.
It is pale lemon to straw, usually 8.5 to 11% alcohol, from Loureiro, Arinto, Trajadura, Avesso and Azal.
Alvarinho from Monção and Melgaço has more alcohol, 11.5 to 14%, and ripe tropical aromas.
Dão reds are ruby, with complex fruit and floral aromas, good structure, soft tannins and good acidity.
The reds age well.
The whites are lemon-colored, with complex fruity and mineral aromas, and are fresh, with good acidity that gives length.
Vines grow mostly on granite, in a region ringed by mountains, with cold, rainy winters and very hot, dry summers.
Alentejo wines taste young, fruity or floral when new, and develop more complex aromas with age.
Reds range from ruby to deep red, and whites from pale lemon to light gold.
Some wine is still made in large clay pots called talhas, a tradition dating back to Roman times.
Alentejano wines are fruity and smooth, with a full, sturdy body.
About 3,000 hours of sun a year favor ripeness and deep color in the grapes.
Young wines are fruity or floral and grow more complex with age.
Lisboa makes a wide range of wines: red, white, rosé, sparkling, fortified and the light Leve.
Lisboa Leve is low in alcohol, with fruity or floral aromas and a tart, fresh taste.
Its Atlantic coast and varied hills, soils and climate account for the range.
